syllabus_topics: I. ATOM-CRYSTALLINE STRUCTURE OF METALS: Structure of the free atom. Nature of interatomic forces. Types of interatomic bonds. Electronic theory of metals. Physical properties of materials determined by atomic structure. Short and long-range order. Crystalline systems and lattices. Crystallographic notations and relationships. Crystalline lattice compactness. Complex crystalline structures. Real crystal structure (point, linear, and surface defects). Atom diffusion in materials (diffusion mechanisms; diffusion rate; diffusion laws; Kirkendall effect; diffusion-based phenomena and applications).

II. METHODS OF STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS AND NON-DESTRUCTIVE TESTING OF MATERIALS: X-ray structural analysis. Non-destructive material analyses: penetrating radiation analysis; ultrasound analysis; magnetic analysis methods; electrical analysis methods; electromagnetic analysis methods; penetrating liquid analysis.

III. SOLIDIFICATION OF METALS: Cooling-heating curves. Solidification thermodynamics. Nucleation. Crystal growth. Solidification kinetics. Tammann's theory of primary crystallization. Ingot structure and primary crystallization defects.
IV. PHASES AND CONSTITUENTS IN METAL ALLOY SYSTEMS: Solid phases in metal alloy systems. Pure components. Solid solutions. Chemical compounds. Mechanical mixtures.

V. EQUILIBRIUM IN METAL ALLOY SYSTEMS: Concepts of thermodynamics of metal alloy systems. Phase rule. Equilibrium diagrams of binary alloy systems. Lever rule. Non-equilibrium states of metal alloy systems. Dependence of physical-mechanical and technological properties on the form of equilibrium diagrams (Kurnakov's law). Ternary alloy systems.

VI. PLASTIC DEFORMATION OF MATERIALS: Plastic deformation of single crystals. Plastic deformation of polycrystalline materials. Cold plastic deformation. Hot plastic deformation. Creep. Superplasticity.

VII. MATERIAL BEHAVIOR IN SERVICE: Material fracture under static loads. Ductile-brittle transition. Fatigue fracture. Fracture mechanics. Oxidation. Corrosion. Behavior of irradiated materials. Wear.

VIII. TRANSFORMATIONS IN SOLID STATE: Homogeneous transformations: order-disorder transformation; spinodal transformation. Heterogeneous transformations: eutectoid transformation; bainitic transformation; martensitic transformation; formation of solid solutions from two-phase mechanical mixtures upon heating; decomposition of supersaturated solid solutions upon heating. Thermokinetic transformation curves of austenite.

IX. FERROUS ALLOYS: Carbon steels: equilibrium diagram, structure, physical-mechanical and technological properties, accompanying elements, classification and standardization. Ordinary white and gray cast irons: equilibrium diagram, technological formation conditions, chemical composition, structure, properties, modified cast irons, malleable cast irons, standardization. Alloy steels and cast irons: influence of alloying elements on Fe, C, phase constituents, critical transformation points, and on austenite during cooling; classification and standardization of alloy steels and cast irons. Iron-based alloys with special properties.
X. HEAT TREATMENTS: Annealing. Normalizing. Hardening. Tempering. Solution hardening and aging. Thermochemical treatments. Thermomechanical treatments.

XI. NON-FERROUS ALLOYS: Alloys based on: copper, aluminum, nickel, magnesium, beryllium, cobalt, zinc, titanium, zirconium. Refractory metal materials. Printing materials. Low melting point materials. Antifriction materials. Dental materials.

XII. SINTERED MATERIALS FROM METAL POWDERS: Obtaining and characteristics of metal powders. Structural transformations during powder pressing. Structural transformations during compact sintering. Structure, properties, uses of sintered metal products.
XIII. AMORPHOUS METAL MATERIALS: Methods for obtaining amorphous metal materials. Structure. Properties. Uses.

XIV. COMPOSITE MATERIALS, CERAMICS, POLYMERS: Technologies for obtaining composite materials. Structure. Properties. Uses. Structure of ceramic materials. Amorphous ceramic materials. Behavior of ceramic materials under load. Obtaining, properties, and applications of ceramic materials. Classification. Structure. Obtaining. Thermoplastic materials. Elastomers (rubbers). Thermoreactive polymers.

Clear and systematic exposition of fundamental notions

Discussions and questions during laboratory works
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the corresponding study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for the exam component (60%) and the laboratory activity component (40%). All laboratory works must be completed, with recovery allowed for only one missed laboratory work.
